spread/spread: How spread out is a random value? Take one that is minus two or two, equally often. Its mean, the average, is zero.
spread/var: The variance is the average squared distance from the mean. Each value sits two away, and two squared is four, so the variance is four.
spread/std: Its square root, the square root of four, is two: the standard deviation, S T D for short. Square a standard deviation to get the variance back.
adds/pair: Now add two independent values, each minus one or one, with variance one. Independent: one tells nothing about the other, so all four pairs are equally likely. Their sums are minus two, zero, zero and two.
adds/adds: Squared, those are four, zero, zero and four, which average to two: one plus one. When independent values add, their variances add.
adds/prod: Multiply instead: a weight of minus two or two, times an independent input of minus one or one. Every product is minus two or two: variance four, which is four times one. With mean zero, variances multiply.
adds/sum: A unit adds up n such terms, inputs times weights. If each has variance v, the sum z has variance n times v, written var of z equals n v, Var for variance.
adds/big: Give a hundred inputs, and their weights, a variance of one. Each term has variance one times one, so the sum has variance a hundred, and a standard deviation of the square root of a hundred: ten.
adds/root: Four times as many terms make the variance four times as big, but the standard deviation only twice as big: twenty-five such terms give a standard deviation of five, and a hundred give ten.
try/p1: Try one. A unit computes z, w dot x, over four hundred inputs, each of variance one. Each weight has a standard deviation of zero point one. What is the standard deviation of z?
try/a1: Square the weight's standard deviation to get its variance: zero point zero one. Times the input's variance, one, each term has variance zero point zero one.
try/b1: Four hundred terms add up to a variance of four. Its square root is the standard deviation: two.
